name: Spartanburg County

actions.title: Rejection of $3 Billion TigerDC / Tyger River Industrial Park Data Center
actions.summary: County council reversed its prior approvals of a $3 billion data center in the Tyger River Industrial Park following sustained community pushback and growing state legislative pressure.

actions.title: One-Year Data Center Development Moratorium — First Reading
actions.summary: County council unanimously passed the first reading of a one-year moratorium on new data center land-use applications, prompted by a permit filed by Lighthouse Data Centers for 300 Jones Road, with two additional readings required for full enactment.

contextBlurb: Spartanburg County has been a focal point of South Carolina's data-center debate throughout 2025–2026, with residents successfully defeating a proposed $3 billion facility and pushing council toward a moratorium. A separate $2.8 billion NorthMark Strategies project at the former Kohler plant — permitted before the moratorium — has drawn hundreds of residents to public hearings over its plan to expand on-site natural gas power generation from ~50 MW to 450 MW, raising air-quality and noise concerns.

name: Colleton County

actions.title: Zoning Code Amendment Permitting Data Centers via Special Exception
actions.summary: County council amended its zoning code in late 2025 to allow data centers as a special exception in rural/light-industrial zones and as a conditional use in heavy-industrial zones, delegating approval authority to the Zoning Board of Appeals.

actions.title: Community Opposition to 1,000-MW Eagle Rock Partners Data Center Campus
actions.summary: Approximately 400 residents packed the Dec. 18 Zoning Board of Appeals meeting to oppose a proposed 1,000-MW, 859-acre data center campus near the ACE Basin; no vote occurred due to a defective meeting notice, and the developer (Eagle Rock Partners) did not refile.

actions.title: SELC Lawsuit Challenging Zoning Code Changes
actions.summary: Residents Miles Crosby and Jennifer Singleton, supported by the Southern Environmental Law Center, sued Colleton County challenging the zoning ordinance changes as inconsistent with the county's comprehensive plan.

actions.title: Six-Month Data Center Development Moratorium — First Reading
actions.summary: County council unanimously advanced a six-month moratorium on all data center land-use approvals to a second reading, aiming to update its comprehensive plan and revise zoning rules in response to community pressure.

contextBlurb: Colleton County became a flashpoint for South Carolina's rural data-center debate after a Charlotte developer proposed converting 859 acres near the environmentally sensitive ACE Basin into a gigawatt-scale data center campus. Around 400 residents mobilized against the project, leading to a legal challenge by the Southern Environmental Law Center and, ultimately, a county-initiated moratorium to pause approvals while the comprehensive plan is updated.

name: Marion County

actions.title: Approval of $2.4 Billion 'Project Liberty' Data Center Under NDA
actions.summary: Marion County council approved a $2.4 billion data center project and fee-in-lieu-of-tax agreement at a meeting held during a winter storm, with the project listed on the agenda only as 'Project Liberty' under a nondisclosure agreement that blocked public disclosure of details until the final vote.

contextBlurb: Marion County quietly approved a $2.4 billion data center project in January 2026 during a major winter storm, with the project shielded from public scrutiny by a nondisclosure agreement and listed only under the codename 'Project Liberty.' Residents voiced anger at the lack of transparency, noting the county's $25 million annual budget made the economic offer difficult to refuse, while also expressing concern about utility costs and long-term impacts on this majority-Black rural community.

name: Newberry County

actions.title: Rejection of County Industrial Park Land Sale to Data Center Developer
actions.summary: Newberry County Council voted down a proposal to sell county-owned industrial park land to a data center developer, then promptly initiated a data center moratorium ordinance.

actions.title: Data Center Development Moratorium Enacted
actions.summary: Newberry County enacted a moratorium ordinance on data center development following council's rejection of a proposal to sell county industrial park property to a data center developer.

contextBlurb: Newberry County moved swiftly to enact a data center moratorium in mid-2026 after county council voted against selling property in a county-owned industrial park to a data center developer. The moratorium is part of a broader wave of county-level pauses across South Carolina aimed at establishing local standards before state-level regulations are finalized.

name: Chesterfield County

actions.title: Data Center Development Moratorium Enacted
actions.summary: Chesterfield County enacted a data center moratorium ordinance in early June 2026, joining a wave of South Carolina counties pausing data center approvals to establish local land-use standards.

contextBlurb: Chesterfield County was among the first South Carolina counties to formally enact a data center moratorium ordinance, doing so in early June 2026 alongside Newberry County. The action reflects a statewide trend of rural and smaller counties seeking to pause development while the General Assembly works toward comprehensive data center oversight legislation.

name: York County

actions.title: Consideration of Local Data Center Regulations Before Any Approval
actions.summary: York County began developing its own local data center regulations proactively before considering any approval, in response to the statewide debate over siting, utility impacts, and community concerns.

contextBlurb: York County proactively moved to develop its own data center regulatory framework before entertaining any approval applications, reflecting growing awareness among South Carolina county governments of the need for local land-use standards. The county's approach mirrors similar regulatory consideration underway in Horry County, as both seek to get ahead of the AI-driven data center development wave.

name: Greenwood County

actions.title: Twelve-Month Data Center Development Moratorium
actions.summary: Greenwood County Council approved Ordinance 2026-25 on third and final reading in a 4-3 vote, blocking new data center approvals for 12 months while the county develops local standards.

contextBlurb: Greenwood County enacted a 12-month pause on new data center approvals on July 21, 2026, after three readings and sustained public debate. Ordinance 2026-25 passed 4-3, giving the county time to develop standards for siting, utility impacts, noise, water use, and environmental protections amid interest from multiple developers.
